newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firm on auction hopes, U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firm on auction hopes, U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso held on to its initial modest gains at late morning dealing on Tuesday due to gains expected in local interest rates late in the day while U.S. long bond yields were down, traders said.
"The peso is firm, due to the Tuesday-effect, with Cetes rates seen up at this evening's auction. The long bond is also bolstering the peso," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart both stood 0.3 centavos firmer at 7.9295/7.9320 and 7.9250/7.9280 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed trade for the day 2.1 centavos firmer at 7.9220/7.9240 per dollar.
